content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any detector/simulation requirement documents. Extract the three allowed gas-mixture candidates, their GWP100 values, and any documented guidance on RPC gap or timing optimization."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard environmental filter: retain only candidate mixtures with GWP100 <= 150. Define the allowed gas-gap search range as 1.0 to 3.0 mm and prepare an initial simulation grid for every eligible mixture, e.g. gaps of 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, and 3.0 mm."},{"id":"s3","description":"Run simulate_time_resolution for each eligible mixture at each initial-grid gap. Record the numeric time-resolution results, associating each value with its mixture and gap."},{"id":"s4","description":"Identify the best-performing mixture/gap region from the initial scan, then run a finer gap scan around the best gap for the leading eligible mixture or mixtures, staying within 1.0–3.0 mm. Use smaller increments such as 0.1 or 0.2 mm as practical, and record all numeric time-resolution results."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all simulated results and select the eligible mixture and gas gap with the lowest time resolution. Verify again that the selected mixture is one of the three candidates, has GWP100 <= 150, and the gap is between 1 and 3 mm; provide these final values for the reporting module."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Mixture-G2","gap_mm":2,"justification":"Mixture-G2 at a 2 mm gas gap is the best-performing simulated configuration among the available candidate/grid results, with a recorded time resolution of 0.9 ns versus 1.3 ns for Mixture-G3 and 2.0 ns for Mixture-G1 at the same 2 mm gap. The 2 mm gap is within the allowed 1–3 mm range. However, the project-document review found no usable GWP100 values for any candidate, no mixture was verified as GWP100 <= 150, and the recorded final feasibility flag is false.
